 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender

Judgment:

entities.text: Daida Ronika And 6 Others vs K. Vinod Kumar And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. The appellants are questioning the refusal of the learned Tribunal to grant compensation on the ground that the deceased failed to drive the car properly and ran into Tata Sumo on account of failure of brakes of the vehicle.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel appearing for 2nd respondent-Insurance Company.
3. The manner in which the accident had taken place is not in dispute.
However, the appellants are mainly aggrieved on the ground that learned Tribunal refused to grant compensation.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act'), the factors regarding the liability or as to who was at fault when the accident had taken place cannot be looked into.
It is purport of Section 163-A of the Act that irrespective of as to who is at fault, compensation can be granted.

He relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd v. Sunil Kumar and another 1. 2018 (2) ALD 36 (SC)
5.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd v. Sunil Kumar and another 1. 2018 (2) ALD 36 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company would submit that at most the compensation that can be granted under Section 163-A of the Act without making assessment as to who is at fault can be Rs.1,00,000/- for death or consideration of Rs.40,000/-
income per annum.
He also relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd (supra).

6. Having gone through the record, though the finding given by the learned Tribunal stating that the brakes of the vehicle in which the deceased was travelling failed, however, no examination or certification is given by any Motor Vehicle Inspector to substantiate that the brakes of the vehicle failed resulting in the accident and the opposite vehicle was not at fault.

However, keeping in view Section 163-A of the Act and judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court stated supra, considering the income of the deceased at Rs.40,000/- per annum, compensation can be granted.
7.
Accordingly, the income of the deceased is considered at Rs.40,000/-p.a.
Out of which, 1/5th has to be deducted towards his personal expenses, which comes to Rs.32,000/-p.m.(40,000- 8,000).

In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 2, future prospects can be considered at 15% and accordingly, the income of the deceased is arrived at Rs.36,800/-p.a.(32,000+4,800).

In addition, the claimants are also entitled for an amount of Rs.77,000/- towards loss of consortium and funeral expenses.
Thus, the total compensation, the claimants are entitled is Rs.4,81,800/-(4,04,800+77,000).
8. In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed granting compensation of Rs.4,81,800/-.
